title: Canonical-prompt corpus smoke orchestrator for streaming + function-calls
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a lightweight, repeatable smoke orchestration harness that runs a curated canonical prompt corpus across streaming, tool/function-call, and structured-output permutations against live endpoints and simulation mode. The harness must provide deterministic fingerprinting where possible, tolerant diffs for known non-determinism, and gate results into CI with a clear signal for breaking API compatibility changes.
test_plan: Assemble canonical prompt corpus (≈120 prompts) covering: single-turn streaming, multi-turn chat with partial-tool-calls, tool-only invocation patterns, structured JSON outputs, nested function calls, and edge-case tokenization inputs.
Implement a test runner that exercises three invocation modes: streaming (chunked frames), non-streaming (batch), and function-call handshake semantics (request -> tool call -> resumed stream).

Capture raw token streams, function call payloads, and final structured JSON outputs for each run and compute canonical fingerprints (sha256 of normalized output) plus tolerant diffs that ignore timestamp/nonce-like fields.
Create mode matrix in CI: runtime variants (runtime-1.22, runtime-1.23, runtime-1.24-rc), model families (rwd-open-*-v1, rwd-compat-*), and network fallbacks (primary region, fallback region).
Add post-processing rules to detect semantic regressions: missing function keys, invalid JSON, changed field types, streaming frame reordering, and missing tool-call handshake steps.
Expose test results to a lightweight dashboard (JSON artifact) and fail CI on high-confidence breaking signals while annotating flaky tests for quarantine.
Provide a dev-mode harness to run locally against simulation endpoints and an infra-mode to run against production staging endpoints with credential gating.
Document runbooks for diagnosing failures: tokenization drift, kernel scheduling-induced ordering differences, and partial-response truncation.
Add an integration job that runs nightly and a required smoke job that runs on relevant PRs touching runtime or API surface code.
Wire up alerting from nightly regressions into the incident channel and tag owning teams automatically.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run the full canonical corpus end-to-end in <30 minutes against a staging cluster under default concurrency.
Fingerprinting plus tolerant diff identifies semantic regressions with >=90% precision in historical test runs.
CI integration exists: PRs touching runtime or API surface trigger the smoke job; failures block merges by policy.
Artifacts (raw payloads + normalized diffs) are stored in the CI build and a stable S3 path for at least 30 days.
On-disk artifacts include an index linking failure examples to the owning repo and suggested bisect steps.
Team runbook documented and linked; first on-call / on-reviewer knows how to triage common failure classes.
Quarantine flow implemented for flaky tests with a reproducible classifier and quarantine metadata.
Performance overhead of the harness when enabled in PR CI is <10% of existing runtime test jobs (configurable concurrency).
No production secrets required for dev-mode runs; staging runs use vaulted credentials with least privilege.
Stakeholders (runtime, api, qa, devex) have reviewed and signed off on the quality thresholds and CI failure policy.
A follow-up plan exists to expand corpus coverage to include tool chaining (3+) and long-sequence KV-cache scenarios in the next cycle.
